solution.p: SOLUTION: We consider x_1 \mbox{Mn}_{2} \mbox{O}_{4} + x_2 \mbox{H}_{2} \mbox{Cl}_{2} \longrightarrow x_3 \mbox{Mn}_{2} \mbox{Cl}_{4} + x_4 \mbox{H}_{4} \mbox{O}_{2} + x_5 \mbox{Cl}_{4}, which implies \begin{array}{rcrcrcrcrcrcr}2 x_1 \amp \amp \amp - \amp 2 x_{3} \amp \amp \amp \amp \amp \amp \amp = \amp 0 \\4 x_1 \amp \amp \amp \amp \amp - \amp 2 x_{4} \amp \amp \amp \amp \amp = \amp 0 \\ \amp \amp 2 x_{2} \amp \amp \amp - \amp 4 x_{4} \amp \amp \amp \amp \amp = \amp 0 \\ \amp \amp 2 x_{2} \amp - \amp 4 x_{3} \amp \amp \amp - \amp 4 x_{5} \amp \amp \amp = \amp 0\end{array} which has augmented matrix \left[\begin{array}{rrrrrr} 2 \amp 0 \amp -2 \amp 0 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ 4 \amp 0 \amp 0 \amp -2 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 2 \amp 0 \amp -4 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 2 \amp -4 \amp 0 \amp -4 \amp 0\end{array}\right] Notice that entries of the augmented matrix share a common factor of 2, so that it is row equivalent to the matrix \left[\begin{array}{rrrrrr} 1 \amp 0 \amp -1 \amp 0 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ 2 \amp 0 \amp 0 \amp -1 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 1 \amp 0 \amp -2 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 1 \amp -2 \amp 0 \amp -2 \amp 0\end{array}\right]. Now row reduce this matrix to get \begin{array}{ccc} \left[\begin{array}{rrrrrr} 1 \amp 0 \amp -1 \amp 0 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ 2 \amp 0 \amp 0 \amp -1 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 1 \amp 0 \amp -2 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 1 \amp -2 \amp 0 \amp -2 \amp 0\end{array}\right] \amp \overset{-4 R_1 + R_2 \Rightarrow R_2}{\sim} \amp \left[\begin{array}{rrrrrr} 1 \amp 0 \amp -1 \amp 0 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 2 \amp -1 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 1 \amp 0 \amp -2 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 1 \amp -2 \amp 0 \amp -2 \amp 0\end{array}\right] \\ \amp \overset{R_2 \Leftrightarrow R_4}{\sim} \amp \left[\begin{array}{rrrrrr} 1 \amp 0 \amp -1 \amp 0 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 1 \amp -2 \amp 0 \amp -2 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 1 \amp 0 \amp -2 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 2 \amp -1 \amp 0 \amp 0\end{array}\right] \\ \amp \overset{-R_2 + R_3 \Rightarrow R_3}{\sim} \amp \left[\begin{array}{rrrrrr} 1 \amp 0 \amp -1 \amp 0 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 1 \amp -2 \amp 0 \amp -2 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 2 \amp -2 \amp 2 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 2 \amp -1 \amp 0 \amp 0\end{array}\right] \\ \amp \overset{-R_3 + R_4 \Rightarrow R_4}{\sim} \amp \left[\begin{array}{rrrrrr} 1 \amp 0 \amp -1 \amp 0 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 1 \amp -2 \amp 0 \amp -2 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 2 \amp -2 \amp 2 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 0 \amp 1 \amp -2 \amp 0\end{array}\right] \end{array} We set x_5 = s_1 as a free variable. From row 4, x_4 - 2 s_1 = 0\Rightarrow x_4 = 2 s_1. From row 3, 2 x_3 - 2 x_4 + 2 s_1 = 0 \Rightarrow 2 x_3 - 2\left(2 s_1\right) +2 s_1 = 0 \Rightarrow x_3 = s_1. From row 2 x_2 - 2 x_3 - 2 s_1 = 0 \Rightarrow x_2 - 2 (1 s_1) - 2 s_1 = 0 \Rightarrow x_2 = 4 s_1. From row 1, x_1 - x_3 = 0 \Rightarrow x_1 - \left(s_1\right) = 0 \Rightarrow x_1 = s_1. We set s_1 = 1 to obtain x_1 = 1, x_2 = 4, x_3 = 1, x_4 = 2, and x_5 = 1, and the balanced equation is \mbox{Mn}_{2} \mbox{O}_{4}+ 4 \mbox{H}_{2} \mbox{Cl}_{2} \longrightarrow \mbox{Mn}_{2} \mbox{Cl}_{4}+ 2 \mbox{H}_{4} \mbox{O}_{2}+ \mbox{Cl}_{4}.

{\bf b} is a linear combination of {\bf a}_1 and {\bf a}_2.

so
